title: Tensor injectivity for a quotient killed by an ideal under flat reduction
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $E$ an $R$-module. Put $JE=\{\sum_{i=1}^n j_i e_i:j_i\in J,\ e_i\in E,\ n\geq0\}$. Use module tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and flat modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $E/JE$ is flat over $R/J$ and the multiplication map $J\otimes_R E\to E$, $j\otimes e\mapsto je$, is injective. Let $V$ be any $R$-module and $U\subseteq V$ an $R$-submodule such that $JV\subseteq U$, meaning $jv\in U$ for every $j\in J$ and $v\in V$. Then the map $U\otimes_R E\to V\otimes_R E$ induced by inclusion is injective. No nilpotence, Noetherian, finite-generation, or proper-ideal hypothesis is imposed; zero rings and zero modules are allowed.

source.place: Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), first proof paragraph: first Tor vanishing for every module annihilated by J, applied to V/U; stated using the injective ideal-multiplication form of the ring-quotient Tor hypothesis.

proof.text: Compute $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R,E)=0$ from the free resolution consisting of $R$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees. Apply the first-variable Tor exact sequence to $0\to J\to R\to R/J\to0$. It gives an injective boundary $\delta:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/J,E)\to J\otimes_R E$ with image the kernel of $J\otimes_R E\to R\otimes_R E$. The isomorphism $R\otimes_R E\to E$, $r\otimes e\mapsto re$, has inverse $e\mapsto1\otimes e$: the two composites are identities by the tensor balancing relation. Under it the last map is exactly the assumed multiplication map. That map has zero kernel, so $\delta$ has zero image and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/J,E)=0$.

source.place: Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), first proof paragraph; Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal); low-degree Tor exactness from Tags 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor) and 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right).

proof.text: Let $A$ be any $R$-module with $JA=0$ and put $S=R/J$. The action $\bar r a=ra$ is independent of the lift $r$ because $JA=0$. Let $F=S^{(A)}$ be the finitely supported functions from the underlying set of $A$ to $S$. Evaluation $p:F\to A$, $(c_a)\mapsto\sum_a c_a a$, is $S$-linear and surjective, since the basis vector at $a$ maps to $a$. Set $K=\ker p$; both $K$ and $F$ are killed by $J$. Apply the free-restriction Tor bound to $R\to S$, degree $1$, module $E$, and index set the underlying set of $A$. Step 1 gives its Tor-vanishing hypothesis, hence $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(F,E)=0$. The first-variable exact sequence of $0\to K\to F\to A\to0$ now gives an injective boundary $\delta_A:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A,E)\to K\otimes_R E$ whose image is $\ker(K\otimes_R E\to F\otimes_R E)$.

source.place: Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), first proof paragraph; Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal); low-degree Tor exactness from Tags 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor) and 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right).

proof.text: Apply the natural quotient-ring tensor isomorphism to the $S$-modules $K$ and $F$: it sends $k\otimes e$ to $k\otimes\bar e$ and $f\otimes e$ to $f\otimes\bar e$, with $\bar e\in E/JE$. Thus the inclusion-induced map of Step 2 is identified with $K\otimes_S(E/JE)\to F\otimes_S(E/JE)$; the square commutes on pure tensors and hence on all tensors. Since $E/JE$ is flat over $S$, the flat tensor exactness lemma applied to $0\to K\to F\to A\to0$ makes this map injective. Consequently $\delta_A$ has zero image; as it is injective, $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(A,E)=0$ for every $A$ killed by $J$.

source.place: Tag 051C (lemma-what-does-it-mean), first proof paragraph; Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal); low-degree Tor exactness from Tags 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor) and 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right).

proof.text: Set $A=V/U$. For $j\in J$ and $v\in V$ one has $j(v+U)=jv+U=0$, because $JV\subseteq U$. Therefore Step 3 gives $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(V/U,E)=0$. Apply the first-variable Tor exact sequence to $0\to U\to V\to V/U\to0$. Exactness at $U\otimes_R E$ says that the kernel of its inclusion-induced map to $V\otimes_R E$ is the image of the zero module $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(V/U,E)$. This kernel is zero, which is the claimed injectivity.

Step 2: for A with JA=0, the free S=R/J presentation F->A and the free-restriction bound (with ring map R->S, j=1, index set A) give Tor_1(F,E)=0 and an injective delta_A.
